renderings.value: The ～にしても grammar point is used to express that even if a certain condition is true or a certain situation occurs, the outcome will not change. It can be translated as 'even if', 'no matter', or 'regardless of' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
Verb-casual + にしても, い-Adjective + にしても, な-Adjective + だにしても, Noun + だにしても
"Even granting/regardless of" - softer, more conversational than たとえ～ても.
Even if it rains, I have to go to school.
Even if she is angry, we can't avoid talking.
Even if this restaurant is expensive, I recommend it because the quality of the food is good.
Even if he is famous, it's rude to talk about his private life.
